title: How early should you arrive at Edinburgh Airport?
author: Matt
cover_image_alt: A bright airport departures hall with check-in desks and flight screens
intro: Two hours is the usual advice for Edinburgh, but the airport's new scanners, Twilight bag drop and Ryanair's earlier bag drop deadline from 10 November all change the sums. Here's how to work out the right time for your flight.
seo_title: How early should you arrive at Edinburgh Airport?
seo_description: When to get to Edinburgh Airport, with the 2-litre liquids rule, Twilight bag drop the night before, Ryanair's 60-minute deadline and the tram.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
For most flights from Edinburgh:

- **Hand luggage only, checked in online, short-haul:** aim to arrive about **2 hours** before your flight. Outside the busiest times, you can often manage with a little less.
- **Dropping a bag, short-haul:** allow **2 to 2.5 hours**, more at peak times.
- **Long-haul, including the USA:** allow **3 hours**.
- **Early morning flights and school holidays:** add 30 minutes to all of these.

These are our suggestions, not airport rules. Your airline's check-in and bag drop closing times are the deadlines that actually matter, and they're in your booking confirmation.

sections.heading: Security is quicker than it used to be
sections.text:
Edinburgh is one of the UK airports with new CT security scanners. When we checked in October 2026, the airport's guidance said:

- You can carry liquids in containers of **up to 2 litres** each, and keep them in your bag.
- Laptops and tablets can also stay in your bag.
- Liquids in vacuum flasks can't be scanned, so empty them first.

That makes the security queue move faster and saves the clear-bag faff. But **check the rules for your return flight**: many airports abroad still apply the 100ml limit, and you may not be able to bring a 2-litre bottle back through security there.

The airport also posts live security queue times on its social media channels. They cover security only, not check-in or passport control, but they're worth a look before you set off.

sections.heading: Drop your bag the night before
sections.text:
Edinburgh's **Twilight bag drop** lets you check in your hold luggage the evening before an early flight, so you can walk straight to security in the morning. When we checked, it was offered by Ryanair, easyJet, Jet2 and British Airways, each with its own hours and rules. The airport's table listed:

- **Ryanair:** 17:00 to 21:00, for flights before 08:00.
- **easyJet:** 16:00 to 20:00.
- **Jet2:** 16:30 to 21:00, for flights before 12:00, and you must have checked in online at least 24 hours before.
- **British Airways:** 16:00 to 20:00, for flights before 12:00.

You'll need to have checked in and have your boarding pass. For Ryanair, everyone on the booking has to be there when you drop the bags. Hours change, so check the airport's Twilight page before you rely on it.

If you live nearby or are staying at an airport hotel, this is the easiest way to make a 6am flight less painful.

sections.heading: Ryanair's new bag drop deadline
sections.text:
Ryanair is Edinburgh's biggest airline for Europe, and from **10 November 2026** it is closing airport check-in and bag drop **60 minutes before departure** across its network, instead of 40 minutes.

- **If you're dropping a bag,** you need to be at the desk at least an hour before take-off, plus queuing time. Our 2 to 2.5 hours allows for that.
- **If you only have hand luggage** and have checked in online, the change doesn't affect you.

EasyJet, Jet2, British Airways and the long-haul airlines set their own deadlines. Long-haul check-in usually closes earlier than short-haul, which is why we suggest 3 hours.

sections.heading: How long to allow, worked out
sections.text:
Here's how the time adds up for a typical summer Saturday flight to [Barcelona](/destinations/barcelona) at 07:00 with one checked bag:

- Bag drop closes 60 minutes before, at 06:00 (Ryanair from 10 November).
- Allow 20 to 30 minutes for the bag drop queue at a busy time.
- Security at peak time can take 20 to 30 minutes, and you need to be at the gate around 30 minutes before departure.

That puts your arrival at about **05:00**, two hours before the flight. Use Twilight bag drop the night before and you could arrive closer to 05:45, with hand luggage only.

For a winter flight to [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife) at midday on a weekday, an hour and a half is often enough with hand luggage only. For a transatlantic flight to [New York](/destinations/new-york), allow the full three hours.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.text:
The airport is about 8 miles west of Edinburgh city centre:

- **Tram:** around 30 to 35 minutes from the city centre. Make sure your ticket covers the airport zone.
- **Airlink 100 bus:** around 30 minutes from Waverley Bridge, traffic permitting, and runs around the clock, which helps for the earliest flights.
- **Car:** there's a charge to use the drop-off zone outside the terminal, and it's cheaper to pay for parking than to linger. Check current prices on the airport's website.

If you're driving from further afield, allow for traffic on the city bypass and M8 at rush hour.

sections.heading: Five ways to make it easier
sections.text:
1. **Check in online** and download your boarding pass before you leave home.
2. **Use Twilight bag drop** for early flights, if your airline offers it.
3. **Check the live security times** before you set off, especially at 5am to 8am, when the early wave of flights leaves.
4. **Book fast track** if you're travelling in the school holidays and short on time. It isn't usually needed outside peak times.
5. **Know your return airport's liquids rules**, so your 2-litre bottle doesn't get binned on the way home.

Still choosing where to fly? Our guide to [where you can fly direct from Edinburgh](/blog/where-can-you-fly-direct-from-edinburgh-airport) covers the routes, and our [December](/destinations/where-to-go-in-december) and [January](/destinations/where-to-go-in-january) pages show what's good for winter sun. Rules and opening hours change, so check the airport and your airline before you go.

faqs.question: Is 2 hours enough at Edinburgh Airport?
faqs.answer: For a short-haul flight with hand luggage only and online check-in, two hours is usually plenty. If you're dropping a bag at a busy time or flying long-haul, allow more.

faqs.question: Has Edinburgh Airport got rid of the 100ml liquids rule?
faqs.answer: When we checked in October 2026, yes. Edinburgh's new scanners let you carry containers of up to 2 litres and keep them in your bag. Rules at your return airport may be different.

faqs.question: Can you drop bags the night before at Edinburgh Airport?
faqs.answer: Yes, with Twilight bag drop for Ryanair, easyJet, Jet2 and British Airways, each with its own evening hours and conditions. Check the airport's website for current times.

faqs.question: How early can you check in at Edinburgh Airport?
faqs.answer: It depends on your airline. Bag drop desks usually open two to three hours before departure, so arriving much earlier than that can mean waiting. Twilight bag drop is the exception.

faqs.question: How long does the tram take to Edinburgh Airport?
faqs.answer: Around 30 to 35 minutes from the city centre. The Airlink 100 bus takes about 30 minutes from Waverley Bridge, depending on traffic.
